questions.question: When using a mirror, you should:

options.text: Stare at the mirror for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors with quick glances. If you look too long, you may travel far down the road without seeing what is ahead of you.

questions.question: When you apply your brakes, the vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, it may have a brake problem.

questions.question: A jogger wearing a stereo headset:

options.text: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.
Can hear the sounds of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around joggers and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle and could do something dangerous because they do not know you are there.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: An example of required emergency equipment is:
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is fully charged.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long or short.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver:

options.text: May use any cell phone while driving.
May only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
May only use a cell phone while driving on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if permitted.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving, it must be hands-free and located close to you. Even hands-free phones can distract you from driving. Know all cell phone laws in the state where you are driving.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: A CMV should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher, unless carrying hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher, unless traveling through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is fully charged.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Pads free of oil or grease
Shoes with oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels. Keep your steering wheel movements very small when using this method.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. Tell the examiner what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three different types: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: When traveling below 40 mph, how much following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same rule but add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller ones.

questions.question: When it is hard to see other vehicles at dawn or dusk, you should:
questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to make yourself more visible.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most new heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most new heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brakes that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern since it is stopped.
Only a concern if passengers are getting off.
A concern whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A concern whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around a stopped bus. There may be passengers nearby. The bus may block your view of passengers or block their view of you.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
When there is extra space on a truck.
Only when hazardous materials exceed 200 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Warning placards must be used whenever a vehicle carries certain hazardous materials. A placarded vehicle must display placards on all four sides.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after driving a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
See if rocks are in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance to check that the lug nuts are still tight.
